**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (凝集素) + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is well-suited for high-pigment and lipid-rich tissues like melanoma due to its strong clearing power and compatibility with a wide range of fluorescent dyes. It preserves endogenous fluorescence while allowing deep penetration of exogenous labels. CD31 (PECAM1) is a specific endothelial marker that identifies vascular networks, while lectin labels the luminal surface of vessels, providing complementary information on vessel structure and continuity. The use of Alexa Fluor 647 and 568 ensures good signal-to-noise ratio and minimal overlap with melanin absorption in the red spectrum.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation and Labeling  
1.1 Incubation with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with blocking solution (10% normal goat serum in PBS) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with primary antibody against CD31 (1:100 dilution in blocking solution) for 48 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with secondary antibody (Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat IgG, 1:200 dilution in blocking solution) for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.7 Wash with PBS for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.8 Incubation with biotinylated lectin (e.g., Griffonia simplicifolia lectin, 1:100 dilution in PBS) for 2 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.9 Wash with PBS for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.10 Incubation with streptavidin-Alexa Fluor 568 (1:200 dilution in PBS) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.11 Wash with PBS for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with FDISCO clearing solution (100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE)) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with FDISCO clearing solution (100% (vol/vol) DBE) for 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.51 RI, e.g., 50% (vol/vol) glycerol in DBE) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.51 RI) for 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) RI-matching solution for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Mounting in RI-matching solution using a low-RI refractive index cover glass or custom chamber for light-sheet or confocal imaging.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD31 (PECAM1)+Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is well-suited for high-pigment and lipid-rich tissues like melanoma due to its strong clearing power and deep penetration of antibodies and dyes. It allows for the use of Alexa Fluor 647, which is compatible with the method and ideal for labeling vascular structures (CD31 for endothelial cells). This choice ensures accurate visualization of vascular architecture in 3D, meeting the scientific goals of analyzing vascular density and complexity.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation and Labeling  
1.1 Incubation with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with blocking solution (10% normal goat serum + 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with primary antibody against CD31 (1:200 dilution in blocking solution) for 48 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS + 0.1% Tween-20 for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with secondary antibody Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:500 dilution in blocking solution) for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.7 Wash with PBS + 0.1% Tween-20 for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.8 Wash with PBS for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 1 (10% (vol/vol) DCM, 10% (vol/vol) tetrahydrofuran (THF), 80% (vol/vol) PBS) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 2 (20% (vol/vol) DCM, 20% (vol/vol) THF, 60% (vol/vol) PBS) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 3 (30% (vol/vol) DCM, 30% (vol/vol) THF, 40% (vol/vol) PBS) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.4 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 4 (40% (vol/vol) DCM, 40% (vol/vol) THF, 20% (vol/vol) PBS) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.5 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 5 (50% (vol/vol) DCM, 50% (vol/vol) THF) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.51 RI, e.g., benzyl alcohol/benzyl benzoate (BABB)) for 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mount the cleared tissue in RI-matching solution within a glass-bottomed dish or custom chamber suitable for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.  
6.2 Ensure the sample is fully immersed in RI-matching solution to minimize optical distortion.  
6.3 Perform imaging using a confocal or light-sheet microscope equipped with appropriate excitation/emission filters for Alexa Fluor 647.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD31 (PECAM1)+Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin+Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is well-suited for high-pigment and lipid-rich tissues like melanoma due to its strong clearing power and ability to support deep antibody penetration. It allows the use of Alexa Fluor dyes, which are compatible with the labeling strategy. CD31 (PECAM1) is a specific marker for endothelial cells, enabling structural vascular network visualization, while Lectin labels functional vascular lumens. This combination enables clear distinction between structural and functional vascular components in the tumor microenvironment.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation and Labeling  
1.1 Incubation with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 2 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Washing with PBS for 3 times, 15 minutes each (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
1.3 Incubation with blocking solution (10% normal goat serum + 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with primary antibody against CD31 (1:200 dilution in blocking solution) for 2 days (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Washing with PBS-T (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 3 times, 15 minutes each (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
1.6 Incubation with secondary antibody Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:500 dilution in blocking solution) for 1 day (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.7 Washing with PBS-T for 3 times, 15 minutes each (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
1.8 Incubation with biotinylated lectin (e.g., Griffonia simplicifolia isolectin B4, 1:100 dilution in PBS) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.9 Washing with PBS for 3 times, 15 minutes each (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
1.10 Incubation with streptavidin-Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500 dilution in PBS) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.11 Washing with PBS for 3 times, 15 minutes each (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 1 (10% (vol/vol) DCM, 10% (vol/vol) tetrahydrofuran (THF), 80% (vol/vol) PBS) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 2 (20% (vol/vol) DCM, 20% (vol/vol) THF, 60% (vol/vol) PBS) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 3 (30% (vol/vol) DCM, 30% (vol/vol) THF, 40% (vol/vol) PBS) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.4 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 4 (40% (vol/vol) DCM, 40% (vol/vol) THF, 20% (vol/vol) PBS) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.5 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 5 (50% (vol/vol) DCM, 50% (vol/vol) THF) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.51 RI, e.g., benzyl alcohol/benzyl benzoate (BABB)) for 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mounting the cleared tissue in RI-matching solution within a glass-bottomed dish or custom chamber for light-sheet or confocal imaging.  
6.2 Ensure no air bubbles are present and that the sample is fully immersed in the matching medium.

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** MACS is an aqueous clearing method that preserves endogenous fluorescent proteins and allows deep penetration of exogenous dyes, which is essential for labeling dense human breast cancer tissue blocks. Pan-Cytokeratin is a specific marker for epithelial cells, including cancer cells, and when labeled with Alexa Fluor 488, it provides high specificity and sensitivity. DAPI is not used due to marker-level cautions indicating incompatibility with Pan-Cytokeratin. The method is compatible with the selected dye, has low toxicity, and can be completed within 24–48 hours, meeting the time constraints for intraoperative or near-intraoperative assessment.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation and Labeling  
1.1 Incubation with 10% (vol/vol) PBS-buffered formaldehyde solution for 30 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.2 Washing with PBS (pH 7.4) for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  
1.3 Incubation with 1% (wt/vol) bovine serum albumin (BSA) in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with anti-Pan-Cytokeratin primary antibody (1:200 dilution in 1% BSA/PBS) for 2 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.5 Washing with PBS (pH 7.4) for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  
1.6 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated secondary antibody (1:500 dilution in 1% BSA/PBS) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.7 Washing with PBS (pH 7.4) for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)

2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol, RI = 1.51) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is well-suited for dense human clinical tissue blocks like breast cancer biopsies due to its high clearing power and ability to support deep antibody penetration. It allows for rapid processing within 24–48 hours, which aligns with the time constraint. The use of Pan-Cytokeratin (a specific marker for epithelial cells) with Alexa Fluor 488 ensures clear identification of epithelial cancer cells, while DAPI provides nuclear counterstaining for structural reference without interfering with the target-specific labeling. This combination supports accurate discrimination between residual cancer cells and non-specific background.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation and Labeling  
1.1 Incubation with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  
1.3 Incubation with 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Wash with PBS for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  
1.5 Incubation with primary antibody against Pan-Cytokeratin (1:200 dilution in blocking buffer) for 48 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.6 Wash with PBS for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  
1.7 Incubation with secondary antibody Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-IgG (1:500 dilution in blocking buffer) for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.8 Wash with PBS for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  
1.9 Incubation with DAPI (1:1000 dilution in PBS) for 30 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.10 Wash with PBS for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether, DBE) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (100% (vol/vol) DBE) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.51 RI, e.g., 50% (vol/vol) glycerol in DBE) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.51 RI) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mount the cleared tissue block in RI-matching solution (1.51 RI) on a glass slide using a coverslip or custom chamber.  
6.2 Ensure the sample is fully immersed in RI-matching solution for optimal imaging clarity.

1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Immunostaining  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (1% BSA in PBS) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody against Pan-Cytokeratin (1:100 dilution in blocking solution) for 16 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 16 hours)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [p63 (anti-p63 antibody, Alexa Fluor 488), CD31 (anti-CD31 antibody, Alexa Fluor 647)]  
**Justification:** MACS is an aqueous clearing method that preserves endogenous fluorescent proteins and supports deep antibody penetration, which is essential for labeling dense clinical tissue like prostate needle core biopsies. It provides good morphological preservation with minimal shrinkage or distortion, critical for accurate 3D reconstruction of glandular architecture. The selected markers—p63 (for basal cell layer) and CD31 (for vascular structures)—allow differentiation between normal and cancerous glands by identifying the presence or absence of the basal layer and visualizing vascular networks. These markers are compatible with MACS and provide sufficient contrast for high-resolution imaging. Lectin was excluded due to marker-level cautions indicating compatibility issues with MACS.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation and Labeling  
1.1 Incubation with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 24 hours at 4 ℃ (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS for 3 × 1 hour at room temperature (RT) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 0.1 M glycine in PBS for 1 hour at RT to quench residual aldehyde groups (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Wash with PBS for 3 × 1 hour at RT (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with blocking solution (10% normal goat serum + 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 1 hour at RT (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-p63 (1:200 dilution in blocking solution), anti-CD31 (1:200 dilution in blocking solution) for 48 hours at 4 ℃ (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.7 Wash with PBS-T (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 3 × 1 hour at RT (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.8 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500), Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) for 24 hours at RT (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.9 Wash with PBS-T for 3 × 1 hour at RT (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.10 Wash with PBS for 3 × 1 hour at RT (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol, RI = 1.40) for 36 hours at RT (Temperature: RT, Time: 36 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI = 1.48) for 12 hours at RT (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol, RI = 1.51) for 12 hours at RT (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching  
3.1 Incubation with MACS-R3 (40 vol% MXDA, 70% w/v sorbitol, RI = 1.52) for 24 hours at RT (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

4 Imaging Preparation  
4.1 Incubation with refractive index matching solution (RI = 1.52) for 24 hours at RT (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Mount the cleared tissue in a glass-bottomed dish filled with RI-matching solution for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [p63 (anti-p63 antibody, Alexa Fluor 488), E-cadherin (anti-E-cadherin antibody, Alexa Fluor 647)]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method with strong clearing power suitable for dense human clinical tissues like prostate needle core biopsies. It allows deep penetration of antibodies and dyes, which is essential for labeling both the basal cell layer (p63) and luminal epithelium (E-cadherin). DAPI was removed due to marker-level cautions for p63, CD3, and CD8. Although uDISCO quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, it is compatible with exogenous fluorophores like Alexa Fluor 488 and 647, making it ideal for immunostaining-based analysis of tumor architecture and Gleason scoring.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 10% normal goat serum (NGS) in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Immunostaining  
2.1 Incubation with anti-p63 antibody (1:100 dilution in 1% NGS + 0.1% Triton X-100) for 48 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with anti-E-cadherin antibody (1:200 dilution in 1% NGS + 0.1% Triton X-100) for 48 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Washing with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  
2.4 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated secondary antibody (1:500 dilution in 1% NGS + 0.1% Triton X-100) for 2 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated secondary antibody (1:500 dilution in 1% NGS + 0.1% Triton X-100) for 2 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.6 Washing with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Delipidation  
4.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (100% DBE) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (100% DBE) for an additional 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

6 Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.51 RI, e.g., benzyl alcohol/benzyl benzoate, 1:1 vol/vol) for 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Mounting the cleared tissue in RI-matching solution within a glass-bottomed dish or coverslip for imaging  
7.2 Imaging using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate excitation/emission settings for Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 channels

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [p63 (anti-p63 antibody, Alexa Fluor 488), CD31 (anti-CD31 antibody, Alexa Fluor 647)]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method with strong clearing power suitable for dense human clinical tissues like prostate needle core biopsies. It allows deep penetration of antibodies and dyes, which is essential for labeling structural markers such as p63 (basal cell layer) and CD31 (endothelial cells). Although uDISCO quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, it is compatible with exogenous fluorophores like Alexa Fluor 488 and 647. The combination of these markers enables visualization of the basal cell layer and vascular structures, which are critical for assessing Gleason scoring features such as tumor infiltration, loss of basal layer, and glandular architecture.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 0.1 M phosphate buffer (pH 7.4) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 0.1 M phosphate buffer containing 0.1% Triton X-100 for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Immunostaining  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% normal goat serum in PBS with 0.1% Triton X-100) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-p63 (1:100 dilution), anti-CD31 (1:100 dilution) in blocking solution for 48 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with secondary antibodies: anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 (1:200 dilution), anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 647 (1:200 dilution) in blocking solution for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Washing  
3.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Repeat step 3.1 three times (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Delipidation  
5.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Clearing  
6.1 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE)) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (1.51 RI, e.g., benzyl alcohol/benzyl benzoate (BABB)) for 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with RI matching solution for 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

8 Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Mount the cleared tissue in RI matching solution within a glass-bottomed dish or custom chamber for light-sheet or confocal imaging.  
8.2 Ensure the tissue is fully immersed in RI matching solution to minimize optical aberrations.

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [p63 + Alexa Fluor 488, CD31 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** MACS is an aqueous clearing method that preserves endogenous fluorescent proteins and allows deep penetration of antibodies and dyes, which is essential for labeling both the prostate glandular structure (via p63) and vascular endothelium (via CD31). It minimizes tissue shrinkage and distortion, which is critical for maintaining the spatial relationships of the needle core tissue. The use of Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 ensures compatibility with MACS and provides distinct fluorescence channels for dual-labeling of adenomatous epithelium and basement membrane/endothelial structures.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation and Labeling  
1.1 Incubation with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Washing with PBS for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  
1.3 Incubation with 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Washing with PBS for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  

2 Immunostaining  
2.1 Incubation with primary antibody against p63 (1:100 dilution in blocking buffer) for 48 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Washing with PBS-T (0.1% Tween-20) for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  
2.3 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated secondary antibody (1:200 dilution in blocking buffer) for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.4 Washing with PBS-T for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  
2.5 Incubation with primary antibody against CD31 (1:100 dilution in blocking buffer) for 48 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.6 Washing with PBS-T for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  
2.7 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated secondary antibody (1:200 dilution in blocking buffer) for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.8 Washing with PBS-T for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  

3 Tissue Optical Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol, RI = 1.40) for 36 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 36 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI = 1.48) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol, RI = 1.51) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with MACS-R3 (40 vol% MXDA, 70% w/v sorbitol, RI = 1.52) for 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Mounting the cleared tissue in MACS-R3 within a glass-bottomed dish or custom chamber suitable for light-sheet or confocal microscopy  
5.2 Ensuring no air bubbles are present under the tissue during mounting  
5.3 Imaging using a confocal or light-sheet microscope with appropriate excitation/emission settings for Alexa Fluor 488 and 647, ensuring z-stack acquisition for 3D reconstruction

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PNAd (anti-PNAd antibody, Alexa Fluor 647), CD31 (PECAM1, anti-CD31 antibody, Alexa Fluor 488)]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is well-suited for clearing small whole lymph nodes due to its strong clearing power and deep penetration of antibodies and dyes. It allows for high-resolution imaging of HEV-specific markers (e.g., PNAd) and pan-endothelial markers (e.g., CD31). The method is compatible with the selected fluorophores and avoids quenching of exogenous fluorescent labels. Nuclear counterstaining is omitted to comply with marker-level cautions for CD19, though Hoechst 33342 was originally included; however, it is not a target-specific marker and is cautioned for use with CD19.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation and Labeling  
1.1 Incubation with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 2 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  
1.3 Incubation with blocking solution (10% normal goat serum + 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-PNAd (1:100, Alexa Fluor 647), anti-CD31 (1:100, Alexa Fluor 488) in blocking solution overnight (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 16–18 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS + 0.1% Tween-20 for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  
1.6 Incubation with secondary antibody (if needed) or directly conjugated primary antibodies (as above) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.7 Wash with PBS + 0.1% Tween-20 for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE)) for 3 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 3 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution for 3 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution for 3 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.51 RI, e.g., 50% (vol/vol) sorbitol in DBE) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mount the cleared lymph node in RI-matching solution on a glass slide using a coverslip sealed with nail polish  
6.2 Store at 4 ℃ until imaging  
6.3 Perform imaging using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate excitation/emission settings for Alexa Fluor 488 and 647

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is well-established for clearing small whole organs like lymph nodes, offering strong clearing power and deep antibody penetration. It is compatible with Alexa Fluor 647, which is essential for labeling CD31 (to identify HEV and vascular structures). DAPI is avoided due to marker-level cautions for CD19, though it is not the target marker here; however, the compatibility of DAPI with uDISCO is marked as 'caution', and its use may interfere with imaging quality or quench endogenous fluorescent proteins. Therefore, DAPI is omitted to ensure optimal labeling and imaging of CD31 (PECAM1), which is critical for identifying HEVs.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation and Labeling  
1.1 Incubation with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 2 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS for 3 times, 15 minutes each (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
1.3 Incubation with blocking solution (10% normal goat serum in PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with primary antibody against CD31 (PECAM1, 1:100 dilution in blocking solution) for 2 days (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS-T (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 3 times, 15 minutes each (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
1.6 Incubation with secondary antibody conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:200 dilution in blocking solution) for 1 day (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.7 Wash with PBS-T for 3 times, 15 minutes each (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
1.8 Incubation with DAPI (1:1000 dilution in PBS) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.9 Wash with PBS for 3 times, 15 minutes each (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 1 (10% (vol/vol) DCM, 10% (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol, 80% (vol/vol) PBS) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

4.4 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 4 (40% (vol/vol) DCM, 40% (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol, 20% (vol/vol) PBS) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.5 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 5 (50% (vol/vol) DCM, 50% (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (benzyl alcohol: 1,2-dimethoxyethane = 1:1, RI ≈ 1.48) for 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mount the cleared lymph node in RI-matching solution within a glass-bottomed dish or custom chamber suitable for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.  
6.2 Ensure no air bubbles are present and that the sample is fully immersed in the matching medium.

**Justification:** uDISCO is well-suited for clearing large, dense tissues like subcutaneous tumors due to its high clearing power and deep antibody/dye penetration. 2.5 Incubation with washing buffer (PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) (Repeat 3 times)  
2.6 Incubation with lectin-Alexa Fluor 568 (1:100 dilution in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.7 Incubation with washing buffer (PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) (Repeat 3 times)  
2.8 Incubation with DAPI (1:1000 dilution in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  
2.9 Incubation with washing buffer (PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) (Repeat 3 times)

4.5 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (50% (vol/vol) DCM, 50% (vol/vol) DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

5.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.51 RI, e.g., 50% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.52 RI, e.g., 60% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.53 RI, e.g., 70% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Incubation with final RI-matching solution (1.54 RI, e.g., 80% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Mounting in a refractive index-matched medium suitable for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD19+Alexa Fluor 647, GL7+Alexa Fluor 568, PNA-Lectin+Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is well-established for clearing whole mouse organs of similar size (15 mm × 10 mm × 5 mm), offering strong clearing power and deep penetration of antibodies and dyes. It is compatible with Alexa Fluor 488, 568, and 647, which are essential for labeling B cells (CD19), germinal centers (GL7), and lectin-based structures (PNA-Lectin). DAPI is used as a nuclear counterstain to assess cell density. The method’s high refractive index matching and solvent-based clearing make it suitable for large, dense tissues like the spleen while preserving morphology.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 0.5 M EDTA in PBS, pH 8.0, for 2 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with 0.1 M Tris-HCl, pH 8.0, for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Immunostaining  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% normal goat serum + 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: CD19 (1:100 dilution), GL7 (1:100 dilution), and PNA-Lectin (1:100 dilution) in blocking solution overnight (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 16–18 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:200 dilution), Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:200 dilution), and Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:200 dilution) in blocking solution for 2 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 dilution in PBS) for 10 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  

3 Washing  
3.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.1% Tween-20 for 10 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  
3.2 Repeat step 3.1 three times (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes each)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Delipidation  
5.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Justification:** uDISCO is well-established for clearing whole mouse organs of similar size and density, offering strong clearing power with good dye penetration. This method allows for deep tissue imaging with minimal distortion, enabling 3D assessment of slit diaphragm integrity across the entire kidney. The use of specific antibodies against Nephrin and Podocin ensures accurate detection of the target structures, while avoiding incompatible nuclear dyes or lectins that could interfere with the signal.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation and Labeling  
1.1 Incubation with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 2 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Washing with PBS for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
1.3 Incubation with blocking solution (10% normal goat serum + 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-Nephrin (NPHS1) (1:200 dilution in blocking solution) and anti-Podocin (NPHS2) (1:200 dilution in blocking solution) for 48 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Washing with PBS + 0.1% Tween-20 for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
1.6 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500 dilution in blocking solution) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-goat IgG (1:500 dilution in blocking solution) for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.7 Washing with PBS + 0.1% Tween-20 for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 1 (10% (vol/vol) DCM, 10% (vol/vol) tetrahydrofuran (THF), 80% (vol/vol) PBS) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 2 (20% (vol/vol) DCM, 20% (vol/vol) THF, 60% (vol/vol) PBS) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 3 (30% (vol/vol) DCM, 30% (vol/vol) THF, 40% (vol/vol) PBS) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.4 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 4 (40% (vol/vol) DCM, 40% (vol/vol) THF, 20% (vol/vol) PBS) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.5 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 5 (50% (vol/vol) DCM, 50% (vol/vol) THF) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.51 RI, e.g., benzyl alcohol/benzyl benzoate (BABB)) for 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mounting the cleared kidney in RI-matching solution within a glass-bottomed dish for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.  
6.2 Ensure no air bubbles are present and the sample is fully immersed in the matching medium.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Podocin (NPHS2) + Alexa Fluor 647, CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 568, Lectin + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is well-established for clearing large, dense soft tissues like the mouse kidney, offering strong clearing power and deep antibody/dye penetration. It supports multi-fluorophore labeling with good compatibility for Alexa Fluor dyes, which are essential for visualizing podocytes (via Podocin), glomerular endothelial cells (via CD31), and vascular structures (via Lectin). The method’s high refractive index matching capability ensures minimal distortion, preserving the 3D architecture of glomeruli for accurate quantification and spatial mapping.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation and Labeling  
1.1 Incubation with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 2 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Washing with PBS for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  
1.3 Incubation with blocking solution (10% normal goat serum in PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with primary antibodies:  
   - Anti-Podocin (NPHS2) (1:200 dilution in blocking solution)  
   - Anti-CD31 (PECAM1) (1:100 dilution in blocking solution)  
   - Lectin (1:50 dilution in blocking solution)  
   (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Washing with PBS-T (0.1% Triton X-100) for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  
1.6 Incubation with secondary antibodies:  
   - Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500 dilution in PBS-T)  
   - Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500 dilution in PBS-T)  
   - Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:500 dilution in PBS-T)  
   (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.7 Washing with PBS-T for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  
1.8 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 dilution in PBS) for 10 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  
1.9 Washing with PBS for 3 × 10 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes each)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 1 (10% (vol/vol) DCM, 10% (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol, 80% (vol/vol) PBS) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 2 (20% (vol/vol) DCM, 20% (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol, 60% (vol/vol) PBS) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 3 (30% (vol/vol) DCM, 30% (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol, 40% (vol/vol) PBS) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.4 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 4 (40% (vol/vol) DCM, 40% (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol, 20% (vol/vol) PBS) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.5 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 5 (50% (vol/vol) DCM, 50% (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.51 RI, e.g., dibenzyl ether or custom RI-matched medium) for 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with RI-matching solution for an additional 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mounting the cleared kidney in RI-matching solution within a glass-bottomed dish or imaging chamber  
6.2 Cover with a coverslip or use a transparent mounting medium to prevent evaporation  
6.3 Ensure the sample is fully immersed in RI-matching solution for optimal light-sheet or confocal imaging

**Chosen Labeling:** [CK19 (导管) + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is well-established for clearing large, dense soft tissues like the mouse liver, offering strong clearing power and deep antibody penetration. It is compatible with Alexa Fluor 488, which is suitable for labeling CK19 (a specific marker for bile duct epithelium). DAPI is avoided due to its incompatibility with CK19 labeling as per the marker-level cautions. This method supports high-resolution imaging of complex 3D structures while minimizing shrinkage and distortion, making it ideal for analyzing spatial distribution patterns of bile duct networks in intact liver lobes.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation and Labeling  
1.1 Incubation with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Wash with PBS for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with primary antibody against CK19 (1:200 dilution in blocking buffer) for 48 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.6 Wash with PBS-T (0.1% Tween-20) for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.7 Incubation with secondary antibody conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500 dilution in blocking buffer) for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.8 Wash with PBS-T for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.9 Incubation with DAPI (1:1000 dilution in PBS) for 30 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.10 Wash with PBS for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE)) for 3 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 3 hours)

4.3 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (100% DBE) for 12 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

5.2 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.48 RI) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) RI-matching solution for 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Mounting in RI-matching solution within a custom chamber or glass-bottom dish for light-sheet or confocal imaging.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Nephrin (NPHS1)+Alexa Fluor 647, Podocin (NPHS2)+Alexa Fluor 568, CD31 (PECAM1)+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is a high-clearing-power solvent-based method suitable for large and dense tissues like the whole mouse kidney. It allows deep penetration of antibodies and dyes, which is essential for visualizing fine structures such as podocyte slit diaphragms and renal glomeruli across the entire organ. The use of Alexa Fluor 488, 568, and 647 ensures compatibility with uDISCO and provides distinct spectral channels for dual labeling of slit diaphragm components (Nephrin and Podocin) and vascular endothelium (CD31). This strategy supports accurate quantification of glomerular number, volume, and morphological changes while preserving tissue geometry.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Immunostaining  
4.1 Incubation with blocking solution (1% BSA in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail:  
   - Nephrin (NPHS1) antibody (1:100 dilution in blocking solution)  
   - Podocin (NPHS2) antibody (1:100 dilution in blocking solution)  
   - CD31 (PECAM1) antibody (1:100 dilution in blocking solution)  
   (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with washing buffer (PBS + 0.1% Tween-20) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) × 3 times  
4.4 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail:  
   - Anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:200 dilution in blocking solution)  
   - Anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 568 (1:200 dilution in blocking solution)  
   - Anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:200 dilution in blocking solution)  
   (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.5 Incubation with washing buffer (PBS + 0.1% Tween-20) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) × 3 times  

5 Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 1 (10% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 2 (20% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 3 (40% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.4 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 4 (60% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.5 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 5 (80% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.6 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 6 (100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (1.51 RI, e.g., benzyl alcohol + benzyl benzoate) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Incubation with mounting medium compatible with RI 1.51 (e.g., refractive index-matched gel or oil) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.2 Mounting on a glass slide with coverslip for light-sheet or confocal imaging.

DAPI was removed due to its caution status for CK19 labeling; instead, nuclear architecture can be referenced through the tissue's intrinsic contrast or alternative non-conflicting nuclear markers if needed. **Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: anti-CK19 (Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated, 1:200 dilution in blocking solution) and anti-CK19 (Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated, 1:200 dilution in blocking solution) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with washing buffer (PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) (Repeat 3 times)  
2.4 Incubation with washing buffer (PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) (Repeat 3 times)  

3 Delipidation

3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Antibody Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with 1:100 dilution of anti-CK19 antibody (Alexa Fluor 488 conjugated) in 100% methanol for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Washing with 100% methanol for 3 × 15 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  

3 Dehydration and Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.3 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (DBE) for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

**Chosen Labeling:** [CK19 (导管) + Alexa Fluor 488, CK19 (导管) + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is well-suited for large, dense, and pigmented tissues like the liver, offering strong clearing power with good dye penetration. It supports dual-color labeling using Alexa Fluor dyes, which are compatible with uDISCO and provide high signal-to-noise ratios for detailed 3D imaging of complex structures such as the biliary tree. CK19 is a specific marker for bile duct epithelial cells, making it ideal for tracing the biliary network. The use of two distinct Alexa Fluor dyes allows for clear separation of signals during imaging and reconstruction.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Immunostaining  
2.1 Incubation with 1% BSA in PBS to block nonspecific binding (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody against CK19 (1:200 dilution in 1% BSA/PBS) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated secondary antibody (1:500 dilution in 1% BSA/PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated secondary antibody (1:500 dilution in 1% BSA/PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.5 Washing with 1% BSA in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 15 minutes)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (10% (vol/vol) DCM, 10% (vol/vol) tetrahydrofuran (THF), 80% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (20% (vol/vol) DCM, 20% (vol/vol) THF, 60% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (30% (vol/vol) DCM, 30% (vol/vol) THF, 40% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.4 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (40% (vol/vol) DCM, 40% (vol/vol) THF, 20% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.5 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (50% (vol/vol) DCM, 50% (vol/vol) THF) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.51, e.g., benzyl alcohol/benzyl benzoate, 1:1 vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.51) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Incubation with 1% (vol/vol) Sudan Black B in RI-matching solution to reduce background autofluorescence (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Washing with RI-matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 15 minutes)  
6.3 Mounting in RI-matching solution for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [α-SMA + Alexa Fluor 568, PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is well-established for clearing whole mouse organs of similar size (10 mm × 8 mm × 5 mm), offering strong clearing power and deep antibody penetration necessary for visualizing dense structures like airway smooth muscle and neural networks. It is compatible with Alexa Fluor 568 and 647, which are suitable for labeling α-SMA (airway smooth muscle) and PGP9.5 (neural markers). The method avoids quenching of exogenous fluorophores when using antibodies, ensuring high signal integrity for 3D imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2 Permeabilization  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol containing 0.5% (wt/vol) Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol containing 1% (wt/vol) Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3 Labeling  
3.1 Incubation with blocking solution (1% BSA in PBS with 0.1% Tween-20) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with primary antibody against α-SMA (1:200 dilution in blocking solution) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 days)  
3.3 Incubation with primary antibody against PGP9.5 (1:200 dilution in blocking solution) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 days)  
3.4 Incubation with secondary antibody conjugated to Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500 dilution in blocking solution) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with secondary antibody conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500 dilution in blocking solution) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.6 Washing with PBS containing 0.1% Tween-20 (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 15 minutes)

4 Delipidation  
4.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

5 Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 1 (10% (vol/vol) DCM, 10% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE), 80% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 2 (20% (vol/vol) DCM, 20% (vol/vol) DBE, 60% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 3 (40% (vol/vol) DCM, 40% (vol/vol) DBE, 20% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
5.4 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution 4 (100% (vol/vol) DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

6 Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.51 RI, e.g., benzyl alcohol/benzyl benzoate (BABB)) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

7 Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Mounting the cleared lung in RI-matching solution within a glass-bottomed dish or custom chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.  
7.2 Ensure no air bubbles are present and that the tissue is fully immersed in the matching medium.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [α-SMA + Alexa Fluor 568, Phalloidin + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is well-established for clearing large, dense, and lipid-rich tissues like the mouse lung, offering strong clearing power and deep antibody/dye penetration. It is compatible with Alexa Fluor 488 and 568, which are suitable for labeling F-actin (via Phalloidin) and α-SMA (a specific marker for airway smooth muscle). The use of Phalloidin provides a structural reference for cell cytoskeletons, while α-SMA ensures specific identification of airway smooth muscle. This combination allows for precise quantification of smooth muscle remodeling in 3D.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 0.1 M phosphate buffer (pH 7.4) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 0.1 M phosphate buffer containing 0.1% Triton X-100 for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Antibody Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with primary antibody against α-SMA (1:200 dilution in blocking buffer) for 48 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 0.1 M phosphate buffer containing 0.1% Triton X-100 for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with secondary antibody Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500 dilution in blocking buffer) for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with 0.1 M phosphate buffer containing 0.1% Triton X-100 for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488 (1:100 dilution in blocking buffer) for 2 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.6 Incubation with 0.1 M phosphate buffer containing 0.1% Triton X-100 for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Delipidation  
4.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) for 3 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  

5 Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (100% DBE) for 48 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  

6 Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.51 RI, e.g., 50% w/v sorbitol in DBE) for 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.2 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.51 RI) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.3 Mounting in RI-matching solution for light-sheet or confocal imaging.

**Chosen Labeling:** [α-SMA + Alexa Fluor 488, SM22α + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is well-established for clearing whole mouse organs of similar size (5–20 mm), offering strong clearing power and deep antibody penetration. It supports the use of Alexa Fluor 488 and 647, which are compatible with α-SMA and SM22α labeling, respectively. This method minimizes background fluorescence while preserving tissue morphology, making it ideal for observing detailed airway smooth muscle remodeling and nerve structures in 3D. The high refractive index of the clearing agent also helps reduce internal scattering and improve imaging depth.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Immunostaining  
4.1 Incubation with blocking solution (1% BSA in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with primary antibody against α-SMA (1:200 dilution in blocking solution) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with primary antibody against SM22α (1:200 dilution in blocking solution) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
4.4 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with secondary antibody Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500 dilution in blocking solution) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.6 Incubation with secondary antibody Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500 dilution in blocking solution) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.7 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether, DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (100% (vol/vol) DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (100% (vol/vol) DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

6 Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (1.51 RI, e.g., benzyl alcohol/benzyl benzoate, 1:1 vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with RI matching solution (1.51 RI) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (1.51 RI) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.2 Mounting in RI matching solution (1.51 RI) in a glass-bottomed dish for light-sheet or confocal imaging.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Insulin + Alexa Fluor 488, PDX1 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is well-established for clearing whole mouse organs of similar size (15 mm × 8 mm × 3 mm), offering strong clearing power and deep antibody penetration. It supports the use of Alexa Fluor dyes, which are compatible with the labeling strategy targeting β-cell markers (Insulin and PDX1). This method allows for high-resolution 3D imaging of the entire pancreas while preserving morphology and enabling precise quantification of β-cell content and spatial distribution.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Immunostaining  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (1% BSA, 10% normal goat serum in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: Insulin (1:200 dilution in blocking solution) and PDX1 (1:500 dilution in blocking solution) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with washing buffer (PBS + 0.1% Tween-20) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) (Repeat 3 times)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500 dilution) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-goat IgG (1:500 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with washing buffer (PBS + 0.1% Tween-20) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) (Repeat 3 times)  

3 Nuclear Staining  
3.1 Incubation with Hoechst 33342 (1:1000 dilution in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with washing buffer (PBS + 0.1% Tween-20) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) (Repeat 2 times)  

4 Delipidation  
4.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (10% (vol/vol) DCM, 10% (vol/vol) tetrahydrofuran (THF), 80% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (10% (vol/vol) DCM, 20% (vol/vol) THF, 70% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (20% (vol/vol) DCM, 20% (vol/vol) THF, 60% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.4 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (30% (vol/vol) DCM, 30% (vol/vol) THF, 40% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.5 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (40% (vol/vol) DCM, 40% (vol/vol) THF, 20% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Refractive Index Matching

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin-Alexa Fluor 568, CD31-Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is well-suited for high-lipid and high-pigment tissues like the placenta due to its strong clearing power and compatibility with a wide range of fluorescent dyes. It preserves endogenous fluorescence while allowing deep penetration of antibodies and lectins. Lectin (e.g., from *Concanavalin A* or *Ulex europaeus*) is ideal for labeling vascular lumens, while CD31 marks endothelial cells, providing structural context. DAPI is used for nuclear counterstaining. This combination enables visualization of both functional perfusion (via lectin) and structural vascular networks (via CD31), which aligns with the goal of mapping perfusion status in the placental villous tree.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation and Labeling  
1.1 Incubation with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Washing with PBS for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Washing with PBS for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Immunostaining and Lectin Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with CD31-Alexa Fluor 647 (1:100 dilution in blocking buffer) for 48 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Washing with PBS-T (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with Lectin-Alexa Fluor 568 (1:100 dilution in blocking buffer) for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.4 Washing with PBS-T for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with DAPI (1:1000 dilution in PBS) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Washing with PBS for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Delipidation  
4.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with FDISCO clearing solution (1:1 v/v DCM:benzyl alcohol) for 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol containing 1% (wt/vol) Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Labeling

Lectin and CD31 are ideal for visualizing functional vascular lumens and endothelial structures, respectively, while DAPI provides nuclear counterstaining. **Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [SYCP3 (anti-SYCP3 antibody, Alexa Fluor 647), DAPI]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is well-established for clearing whole mouse organs of similar size and complexity, offering strong clearing power with good dye penetration. It supports the use of antibodies and synthetic fluorophores like Alexa Fluor 647, which are essential for labeling specific targets such as SYCP3 (a marker for meiotic prophase I, critical for identifying spermatocytes in meiosis). DAPI is used for nuclear counterstaining to provide context on cell layers and morphology. The method’s high refractive index matching and solvent-based clearing allow deep tissue penetration while minimizing distortion, which is crucial for preserving the complex architecture of coiled seminiferous tubules.

**Protocol Steps:**

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DDX4 (anti-DDX4 antibody, Alexa Fluor 488), SYCP3 (anti-SYCP3 antibody, Alexa Fluor 647), Hoechst 33342]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is well-established for clearing whole mouse organs of similar size and density, offering strong clearing power with good dye penetration. It supports the use of fluorescently labeled antibodies for target-specific detection of germ cells (DDX4) and meiotic cells (SYCP3), while Hoechst provides nuclear counterstaining for cell layer identification. The solvent-based nature of uDISCO allows compatibility with a wide range of fluorophores, including Alexa Fluor 488 and 647, which are essential for distinguishing germ cell populations and meiotic stages.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2 Immunostaining  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% BSA in PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-DDX4 (1:200 dilution in blocking solution) and anti-SYCP3 (1:200 dilution in blocking solution) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with washing buffer (PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) × 3 times  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500 dilution) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with washing buffer (PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) × 3 times  

3 Nuclear Staining  
3.1 Incubation with Hoechst 33342 (1:1000 dilution in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with washing buffer (PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) × 3 times  

4 Delipidation
