**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 4% PFA in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 10% normal goat serum in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Immunostaining  
2.1 Incubation with Ki67 (MKI67) primary antibody (1:200 dilution in PBS + 1% BSA) for 2 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated secondary antibody (1:500 dilution in PBS + 1% BSA) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with PCNA primary antibody (1:200 dilution in PBS + 1% BSA) for 2 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated secondary antibody (1:500 dilution in PBS + 1% BSA) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with DAPI (1:1000 dilution in PBS) for 10 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  

3 Washing  
3.1 Incubation with PBS for 10 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  
3.2 Repeat step 3.1 three times  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol, RI = 1.40) for 36 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 36 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI = 1.48) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol, RI = 1.51) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

5 Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Incubation with 1x MACS-R2 solution for 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours) to ensure full RI matching  
5.2 Mounting on a glass slide with a coverslip using MACS-R2 as immersion medium for imaging

2.3 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.4 Wash with PBS-T for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)

2.2 Washing with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 15 minutes)

3.1 Incubation with primary antibody against CD31 (PECAM1) at 1:100 dilution in blocking buffer (1% BSA in PBS) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: overnight)  
3.2 Washing with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 15 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with secondary antibody Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat IgG at 1:200 dilution in blocking buffer (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Washing with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 15 minutes)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) sucrose in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)

4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) sucrose in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato, F-Actin + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** MACS is an aqueous clearing method that preserves endogenous fluorescent proteins like tdTomato, which is critical for tracking long-range projections. It also allows deep penetration of exogenous dyes such as Alexa Fluor 488 conjugated to phalloidin for labeling F-Actin (axonal cytoskeleton). This method avoids the use of organic solvents that could quench tdTomato and provides good RI matching for light-sheet imaging with minimal shrinkage.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Wash with PBS for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  

2 Immunostaining for F-Actin  
2.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated phalloidin (1:100 dilution in PBS) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Wash with PBS for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  

3 Optical Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol, RI = 1.40) for 36 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 36 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI = 1.48) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol, RI = 1.51) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with MACS-R3 (40 vol% MXDA, 70% w/v sorbitol, RI = 1.52) for 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Mount the cleared brain in a refractive index-matched solution (MACS-R3) within a custom glass chamber suitable for light-sheet microscopy.  
5.2 Ensure no air bubbles are present and cover the sample with a coverslip or transparent film.  
5.3 Perform imaging immediately or store at 4 ℃ in the matching solution for up to 48 hours before imaging.

**Justification:** uDISCO is well-suited for thick tissue blocks (0.5–3 mm) like the mouse apex tissue, offering strong clearing power and deep antibody penetration. This combination allows clear distinction between vascular smooth muscle and fibrotic myofibroblasts while preserving structural details for 3D reconstruction.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation and Fixation  
1.1 Incubation with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Washing with PBS for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization  
2.1 Incubation with 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Washing with PBS for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Immunostaining  
3.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: α-SMA (1:200 dilution) and PDGFRα (1:200 dilution) in blocking buffer (5% BSA in PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100) for 48 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
3.2 Washing with PBS for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-goat IgG (1:500) in blocking buffer for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.4 Washing with PBS for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Delipidation  
5.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Clearing  
6.1 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE)) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (100% DBE) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.51 RI, e.g., 50% (vol/vol) glycerol in DBE) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.51 RI) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

8 Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Mounting the cleared tissue in RI-matching solution (1.51 RI) on a glass slide using a coverslip sealed with nail polish or optical-grade adhesive  
8.2 Imaging using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate excitation/emission settings for Alexa Fluor 488 and 647

2.2 Wash with PBS for 3 × 10 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  
2.3 Incubation with secondary antibody Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG at 1:500 dilution in blocking buffer for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Wash with PBS for 3 × 10 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  
2.5 Incubation with primary antibody against Podocin (NPHS2) at 1:200 dilution in blocking buffer for 2 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.6 Wash with PBS for 3 × 10 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  
2.7 Incubation with secondary antibody Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-goat IgG at 1:500 dilution in blocking buffer for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.8 Wash with PBS for 3 × 10 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Delipidation  
4.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (10% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE), 10% (vol/vol) tetrahydrofuran (THF), 80% (vol/vol) PBS) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (20% (vol/vol) DBE, 20% (vol/vol) THF, 60% (vol/vol) PBS) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (40% (vol/vol) DBE, 40% (vol/vol) THF, 20% (vol/vol) PBS) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (100% (vol/vol) DBE) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.51 RI, e.g., 100% (vol/vol) DBE) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

7 Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Mount the cleared tissue in RI-matching solution on a glass slide using a coverslip.  
7.2 Ensure the sample is fully immersed in RI-matching solution to minimize light scattering.  
7.3 Perform 3D imaging using a light-sheet or confocal microscope optimized for Alexa Fluor 568 and 647 excitation/emission wavelengths.

**Chosen Labeling:** [CD19+Alexa Fluor 488, PNA-Lectin+Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** MACS is an aqueous clearing method that preserves endogenous fluorescent proteins and is compatible with a wide range of fluorophores, including Alexa Fluor 488 and 647. It provides good dye penetration into dense tissues like lymph nodes, supports minimal shrinkage, and avoids the use of hazardous organic solvents. CD19 is a specific B-cell marker for delineating follicles, while PNA-Lectin labels germinal centers, making this labeling strategy ideal for visualizing both structures in 3D light-sheet imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation and Fixation  
1.1 Incubation with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 2 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  

2 Permeabilization  
2.1 Incubation with 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Wash with PBS for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  

3 Immunostaining  
3.1 Incubation with CD19 antibody (1:100 dilution in blocking buffer) for 2 days (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
3.2 Wash with PBS for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  
3.3 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated secondary antibody (1:200 dilution in blocking buffer) for 1 day (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.4 Wash with PBS for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  
3.5 Incubation with PNA-Lectin (1:100 dilution in blocking buffer) for 1 day (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.6 Wash with PBS for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  
3.7 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated secondary antibody (1:200 dilution in blocking buffer) for 1 day (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.8 Wash with PBS for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  

4 Tissue Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol, RI = 1.40) for 36 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 36 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI = 1.48) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol, RI = 1.51) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with MACS-R3 (40 vol% MXDA, 70% w/v sorbitol, RI = 1.52) for 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mount the cleared tissue in MACS-R3 (RI = 1.52) using a glass-bottomed dish for light-sheet microscopy.  
6.2 Ensure no air bubbles are present under the tissue before imaging.

**Chosen Labeling:** [Stabilin-2+Alexa Fluor 647, Lyve-1+Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is well-suited for large, dense tissues like the whole mouse liver, offering strong clearing power and good dye penetration. It preserves fluorescent signals from antibodies, which is critical since endogenous fluorescent proteins (e.g., GFP) are quenched in this method. Stabilin-2 and Lyve-1 are specific markers for liver sinusoidal endothelial cells (LSECs), ensuring accurate labeling of the hepatic vascular network without relying on pan-endothelial markers like CD31. Alexa Fluor 568 and 647 are compatible with FDISCO and provide distinct channels for dual labeling.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation and Fixation  
1.1 Incubation with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Washing with PBS for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization  
2.1 Incubation with 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Washing with PBS for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Blocking and Antibody Labeling  
3.1 Incubation with 5% normal goat serum (NGS) in PBS with 0.1% Triton X-100 for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Stabilin-2 (1:200 dilution) and anti-Lyve-1 (1:200 dilution) in blocking solution for 48 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
3.3 Washing with PBS with 0.1% Triton X-100 for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500 dilution) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500 dilution) in blocking solution for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.5 Washing with PBS with 0.1% Triton X-100 for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Delipidation  
5.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Clearing  
6.1 Incubation with FDISCO clearing solution (100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE)) for 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with FDISCO clearing solution for an additional 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.48 RI, e.g., 100% (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol) for 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with RI-matching solution for an additional 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

8 Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Mounting the cleared liver in a glass-bottom dish filled with RI-matching solution  
8.2 Ensuring no air bubbles are present under the tissue before imaging  
8.3 Imaging using light-sheet microscopy with appropriate excitation/emission settings for Alexa Fluor 568 and 647

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD11b + Alexa Fluor 647, CD3 + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is an established method for hard tissues like bone, offering strong clearing power and deep antibody penetration, which is essential for visualizing immune cells within dense mineralized structures. It supports the use of fluorescently labeled antibodies (e.g., Alexa Fluor 488 and 647) for dual-color immunostaining of pan-immune (CD3) and myeloid (CD11b) subsets. Although it uses organic solvents, its compatibility with these dyes and ability to clear thick tissue makes it ideal for this application.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Immunostaining  
4.1 Incubation with blocking solution (1% BSA in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-CD11b (1:100 dilution in blocking solution) and anti-CD3 (1:100 dilution in blocking solution) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with washing buffer (PBS + 0.1% Tween-20) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:200 dilution in blocking solution) and Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:200 dilution in blocking solution) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 0.5 M EDTA in PBS, pH 7.4, for 48 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with 10% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Immunostaining  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (1% BSA + 10% normal goat serum in PBS) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with anti-Osteocalcin antibody (1:100 dilution in blocking solution) for 48 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated secondary antibody (1:200 dilution in blocking solution) for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated Lectin (1:100 dilution in PBS) for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.6 Incubation with 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Dehydration and Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with 10% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) DBE in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) DBE in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) DBE in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) DBE in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.6 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) DBE in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.7 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) DBE in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.8 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) DBE in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.9 Incubation with 90% (vol/vol) DBE in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.10 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (FDISCO RI-matching reagent, RI = 1.48) for 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with fresh RI-matching solution for 48 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  

5 Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Incubation with 10% (vol/vol) glycerol in RI-matching solution for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) glycerol in RI-matching solution for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) glycerol in RI-matching solution for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) glycerol in RI-matching solution for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.5 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) glycerol in RI-matching solution for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.6 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) glycerol in RI-matching solution for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.7 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) glycerol in RI-matching solution for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.8 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) glycerol in RI-matching solution for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.9 Incubation with 90% (vol/vol) glycerol in RI-matching solution for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.10 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) glycerol for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
